name: Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnosis Criteria for Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple cutaneous adnexal tumors including cylindromas, trichoepitheliomas, and spiradenomas
Positive family history of similar adnexal tumors consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the CYLD gene
Histopathological confirmation of cylindroma, trichoepithelioma, or spiradenoma from skin biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple characteristic cutaneous adnexal tumors with histopathological confirmation; genetic testing and family history support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for CYLD mutations is confirmatory but not mandatory if clinical and histopathological features are definitive.

laboratory: Histopathology showing basaloid tumor islands with hyaline sheaths characteristic of cylindromas
Immunohistochemistry positive for markers such as CK7 and EMA in tumor cells
imaging: MRI or CT may be used to assess extent of large scalp tumors
Ultrasound for evaluation of nodules in parotid gland if suspected
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in CYLD gene on chromosome 16q12-q13
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical examination revealing multiple adnexal tumors

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple cylindromas without trichoepitheliomas
Similar genetic basis but distinct clinical presentation
Extensive scalp cylindromas forming turban-like masses
May overlap clinically but usually without trichoepitheliomas

redFlags: Rapid growth or ulceration of scalp tumors suggesting malignant transformation
Painful nodules indicating possible spiradenoma involvement
Family history of similar tumors indicating inherited syndrome
references: Bignell GR, et al. Identification of the familial cylindromatosis tumour-suppressor gene. Nat Genet. 2000.
Tucker T, et al. Brooke-Spiegler syndrome: a clinical and molecular review. Br J Dermatol. 2004.
Orphanet: Brooke-Spiegler syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
